A calm body with this on the hood only: otherwise too busy
Numbers need a solid black or red plate with a gold outline; gold ones disappear into the brocade.
Almost nothing: it is finished artwork, a plate for numbers
Pairs well with: black, deep red, gold, cream.
pitfalls: Not dragon-scale damask in orange: the render is figurative dragons, coins and gems on red
Not a plain gold metal: the gold is linework and the ground is red lacquer
Avoid: small numbers lost in scale pattern, next to other gold or orange finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 195 (true metallic), roughness 50 (high gloss), clearcoat 31 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers lost in scale pattern, next to other gold or orange finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: it is finished artwork, a plate for numbers; a solid red or black panel behind numbers: the only calm area
Patterns to avoid: any texture or pattern: it buries the dragon detail; flake or glitter: the gems and gold already sparkle
Spec overlays that work: leave spec alone: the metal gold and glossy lacquer split is the design; no extra sparkle: already at maximum
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
